about: Forge Desktop on each operating system (Relay task 130, 2026-10-09). Per OS: the host that shows the page, where each kind of data comes from (tried in order; the first that works wins) and what is cut there, each with its reason. A feature is cut when the OS entry cuts it or when none of its providers works on the machine (no loopback sound device on a Mac, say); a cut feature's widgets and settings are hidden by the page and the settings window (desktop/host/registry.py turns this into the page's caps). Adding an OS or a provider: one module in desktop/host/sources/ plus one line here.

scenery.label: Particles and the visualiser behind the desktop icons

settings_groups: On the desktop: particles, widgets, visualiser
help_about: Per setting, the help text the settings window shows in place of forge_theme's, which is written for Forge on Linux (GNOME, Hyprland, the extension, Forge's pop-out). Each entry: OS name (or * for every OS) -> text; an OS with no text keeps forge_theme's.

desktop_particles.windows: The same particles on your normal desktop, behind every window; clicks go straight through.
desktop_particles.macos: The same particles on your normal desktop, behind every window; clicks go straight through.

desktop_widgets.*: Your widgets on the normal desktop, behind every window, with their own layout. The Widgets button in the corner of the desktop adds, moves and removes them.

desktop_all_screens.*: With more than one screen plugged in, each one shows the particles, the visualiser and its own widgets behind its windows. Off keeps them to the main screen.

desktop_edit_button.*: A small button at the bottom right of the desktop that starts editing the desktop's widgets. Off hides it; Edit widgets at the top of these settings still starts editing.
desktop_edit_button.linux: A small button at the bottom right of the desktop that starts editing the desktop's widgets. Off hides it; Edit widgets at the top of these settings, or the GNOME extension's top bar menu, still starts editing.

desktop_visualiser.windows: Draws whatever the computer is playing on the normal desktop, behind every window. Listens to the sound card's own output only while something draws.
desktop_visualiser.macos: Draws whatever the Mac is playing on the desktop. A Mac can't listen to its own sound by itself: it needs a loopback sound device such as BlackHole set up, and without one this stays hidden.

desktop_particle_fps.*: How many times a second they move. 30 looks smooth and uses about half the power of 60.

partial_about: Per OS, what works only in part there, as plain sentences for that OS's README (registry.change_list prints them after where the data comes from).

windows.label: Windows

cut_settings.desktop_panel_icon: a button in GNOME's top bar; on Windows the settings open from the corner button or the Start menu

partial: Music players: no volume, no Go to player button and no album art; Windows' media controls do not give them.
System widgets: no temperatures, fans, graphics card or Wi-Fi name.
The particles never thin out part way (windows half over the desktop, a busy graphics card): they run in full, or rest while the desktop is covered.
One wallpaper for every screen; a wallpaper set to span the screens fills each one instead.

macos.label: macOS

cut_settings.desktop_panel_icon: a button in GNOME's top bar; on a Mac the settings open from the corner button or the app itself
cut_settings.desktop_particles_rest: on a Mac the page pauses by itself while windows cover the desktop

partial: Particles and the visualiser are drawn just above the desktop icons, not under them (macOS has no place for an app between the wallpaper and the icons); clicks still go through.
Music players: only Music and Spotify, while they are open (macOS 15.4 and later stop apps reading other players).
The visualiser needs a loopback sound device such as BlackHole; without one it stays hidden.
System widgets: no temperatures, fans, graphics card or Wi-Fi name.
The particles never thin out part way (windows half over the desktop, a busy graphics card): they run in full, or rest while the desktop is covered.

provider_labels.gsmtc: Windows' media controls (the players Windows shows in its volume pop-up)
provider_labels.applescript: AppleScript, for Music and Spotify while they are open
provider_labels.soundcard: the sound card's loopback (soundcard library, numpy FFT)
